steps.action: Core validates the project state, repository snapshot, policies, adapter chain, options, and grants.
steps.expectedOutcome: Discovery starts only from exact approved context and a drift-free repository state.

steps.action: The native inventory adapter inspects the allowed local repository surface and optional analyzers contribute bounded observations.
steps.expectedOutcome: Every observation retains exact method, source, confidence, and native provenance.

steps.action: Trusted validation normalizes observations, identifies gaps, and determines whether the candidate can reach the discovery Gate.
steps.expectedOutcome: Material uncertainty blocks; non-material uncertainty remains visible for explicit Gate disposition.

userJourneys.outcome: The configured local target either advances atomically to an evidenced post-state or remains unchanged with an explicit conflict, drift, or failure artifact.

steps.action: Core binds the exact verification approval, verified change, target repository snapshot, target ref, expected commit, and integration policy.
steps.expectedOutcome: No caller or adapter can substitute the subject or integration target.

steps.action: Core compares the live target ref to the expected commit and invokes the configured local Git integration adapter only when they match.
steps.expectedOutcome: Concurrent work serializes and stale work cannot mutate the shared target.

steps.action: Core validates the effect receipt and either records the exact integrated post-state or returns an immutable no-mutation failure artifact.
steps.expectedOutcome: Only proven integration creates completion facts and unlocks frontier recalculation.

risks: A Godot compatibility claim can drift if engine, plug-in, test framework, adapter, or Windows versions are not pinned together.
A conflict resolver could silently create new unverified implementation bytes.
A consistency reviewer may be mistaken for authority unless reviewer findings remain advisory inputs to the Gate.
A crash between Git mutation and checkpoint persistence could duplicate or lose integration evidence.
A declared package export may remain absent from the packed artifact unless verification derives required files from package.json itself.
A facade can accidentally hide authority-relevant decisions or create an implicit bypass path.
A human-readable report may become misleading if missing measurements are silently treated as zero.
A numerical closure score can create false assurance unless all blocking domains and contradictions remain independent hard gates.
A passing check subset could hide an uncovered verification-plan obligation.
A quick profile can be mistaken for completed assurance unless deferred obligations remain explicit and blocking at final acceptance.
A readiness receipt can become stale between verification and execution unless exact fingerprints and upstream identities are revalidated at the execution boundary.
A reporting service may accidentally acquire workflow authority unless its read-only boundary is enforced.
A session snapshot can become hidden global state unless every ModuleInvocation still binds its exact required artifacts.
A stale frontier could run work before prerequisites are integrated.
A user can close a Desktop task without a host callback unless open-session checkpoints and next-task recovery fail closed.
A verified candidate could be mistaken for an integrated or system-accepted change.
A verified change may be applied to target bytes other than those it was verified against.
Adapter performance comparisons may be invalid when inputs, policies, hosts, or circuit versions differ.
Adapter-native semantics may leak into canonical contracts unless conformance remains strict.
Ambiguous edge direction could duplicate inverse facts.
An executor could exceed scope unless the host enforces exact grants.
An executor or verifier could self-certify completeness or independence.
An integrated change could be mistaken for system verification or business acceptance.
Analyzer silence could be mistaken for proof that an architecture element or relationship does not exist.
Analyzer silence could be mistaken for proof that no dependency is missing.
Automated memory extraction can convert inference into false project truth unless every record carries authority, source, confidence, and approval state.
Automatic idea detection can become noisy or silently expand scope unless user confirmation and RoadmapGate authority remain explicit.
Automatic preparation can damage or destabilize a machine unless project-local changes, exact grants, rollback, and global-change approval are enforced.
Compatibility claims can be wrong if compared against a stale ContractBaseline.
Compatibility shims can become permanent accidental API unless removal timing and migration evidence are enforced.
Concurrent worker conclusions can overwrite one another unless optimistic baseline identity and one serial integration owner are mandatory.
Conditional routing may become implicit unless every condition remains state-driven and evidence-bound.
Context slices may omit a semantically relevant source region unless Gate coverage checks remain independent of proposer selection.
Contract-format special cases in Core could prevent module and tool replacement.
Cross-platform CI may pass while the release-defining Windows Desktop host path remains untested.
Duplicating TraceabilityGraph into provider memory can drift or create inverse authority unless only trusted checkpointed projections are indexed.
Environment fingerprints can leak secrets or unstable host details unless they use explicit redaction and profile-scoped canonical fields.
Evidence could be valid but refer to different candidate bytes.
Execution could improperly claim verification or integration authority.
External evidence can become unavailable or detached from source claims unless manifests, hashes, and retrieval checks are mandatory.
External planning adapters can drift from the authoritative baseline unless synchronization is bounded, versioned, and conflict-aware.
Frequent conclusion approval can create fatigue unless deltas are concise, complete, grouped by authority, and empty changes remain cheap.
Frontier completion may unlock dependent work too early unless only verified integrated-completion facts affect readiness.
Gate proliferation may add friction unless quick paths remain clear and policy is risk-adjusted.
Generated, ignored, or secret-bearing files could be inspected or transmitted beyond approved policy.
Generator self-certification could admit malformed or semantically incomplete contracts.
GitHub owner-only repository settings may remain incomplete even when source changes and local verification pass.
Graphology traversal or serialization order may leak nondeterminism unless Core canonicalizes all externally visible artifacts and diagnostics.
Hidden adapter-selected context could violate deterministic invocation contracts.
Inferred current state could be mistaken for approved intended architecture.
Instrumentation can add overhead or nondeterminism unless timing and unavailable host observations are modeled explicitly.
Language-specific analyzer semantics could leak into the provider-neutral snapshot contract.
Mandatory bootstrap can add friction or block recovery unless read-only inspection and RoadmapNotInitialized have explicit routes.
Mem0 indexing or model-backed extraction can be nondeterministic, stale, unavailable, or transmit data unless exact configuration, receipts, local defaults, and native equivalence are enforced.
Module boundaries may drift into duplicated responsibility unless every contract keeps one primary purpose.
Non-native host attestations can create false confidence unless policy constrains issuer, type, freshness, and scope.
OPA policy success may be mistaken for semantic completeness unless WorkDependencyGate separately reviews missing-dependency evidence.
Operational telemetry may leak secrets or sensitive logs unless report projection applies explicit content policy.
Parallel checks can race over shared mutable state unless only independent read checks run concurrently and effects remain serialized or isolated.
Priority scores can imply false objectivity unless weights, inputs, confidence, rationale, and ties remain visible.
Provider-specific binding details could leak into generic workflow semantics.
Raw provider output, logs, screenshots, or test receipts can contain secrets, personal information, or unsafe repository content.
Recency weighting can override durable decisions unless authority precedence is evaluated before ranking.
Repository drift could bind findings to a different implementation than the snapshot claims.
Retries could destroy evidence if attempts are overwritten.
Reused task adapters could blur decomposition and dependency authority.
SQLite, worktree, and executor crash windows can create split-brain state unless commit protocols and recovery semantics are explicit.
Stacked pull requests can drift or duplicate evidence unless each change pins its exact parent and lifecycle package.
Stored execution waves could couple static dependencies to changing runtime state.
Technology-specific adapters can create hidden Core special cases unless capability-oriented ports and conformance suites remain mandatory.
Traceability may become incomplete when future contributors omit required lifecycle relationships or evidence horizons.
Upstream tools can change commands, licenses, telemetry, compatibility, or artifact shapes after a version is evaluated.
Verification retries could overwrite failing evidence.
WorkBreakdown can propagate invalid scope if it starts before ContractGate resolution.

sourceRefs.location: All 24 recommendations approved in wave RQW-0FEF4753B3072E01

content.objective: Prove the exact environment required by approved work is safely prepared and currently ready before WorkExecution begins.

scope.boundary: DevRelay EP-001 environment profile, preparation, readiness, evidence, and execution-authorization boundary.

content.problemSummary: A valid work plan and assignment do not prove that required runtimes, tools, services, configuration, permissions, and target facts are present or safe to use.
content.solutionSummary: Add profile-based EnvironmentPreparation plus Core-owned fingerprinting, effect checkpoints, EnvironmentVerificationGate, readiness binding, and trusted traceability.
behaviorFlows: Core resolves the exact host and project profiles after SpecialistAssignmentGate.
Native and optional inventory adapters observe current state without readiness authority.
The planner consolidates all required gaps and presents effects, grants, impact, rollback, and evidence.
Approved capability adapters execute project-local effects and checkpoint each result.
Core fingerprints current state and EnvironmentVerificationGate evaluates exact required and optional evidence.
The readiness binder revalidates and authorizes one execution attempt.
Every later frontier repeats fingerprint validation; drift creates a new immutable remediation cycle.
dataResponsibilities: EnvironmentProfile declares required and optional facts.
EnvironmentBaseline owns approved profiles and policy.
EnvironmentFingerprint is a redacted deterministic current-state identity.
EnvironmentRemediationPlan owns proposed effects but no authority.
EnvironmentReadinessReceipt is Gate-owned and single-attempt bound.
Raw receipts preserve exact observations and effects without secret values.
failureHandling: Unknown or failed required checks block.
Missing grants, rollback, provenance, or adapters returns remediation or unable-to-proceed.
Crash recovery uses exact effect checkpoints.
Drift and expiry create a new attempt.
No silent online fallback or global mutation.
securityPrivacy: Secret references and presence metadata only.
Adapters cannot access TraceabilityGraph or Gate authority.
performanceReliabilityOperability: Independent read checks may run with bounded parallelism.
Per-check duration, retries, cache hits, and bottlenecks are receipted.
No universal V1 wall-clock SLA is asserted.
compatibilityMigrationRollout: Introduce EnvironmentNotInitialized for the current project.
Establish the first profile baseline from the Windows host and EP-001 work requirements.
Enable optional technology adapters only after conformance and live attestation.
Insert revalidation before every WorkExecution frontier without changing static dependency DAG authority.
verificationIntent: Permission, secret, network, path, rollback, crash, and replay matrices.
Fingerprint drift and single-use receipt tests.
Full Desktop prepare, execute, drift, remediate, reverify, and replay dogfood.

elements.name: DevRelay
elements.description: Deterministic orchestration runtime for composable software-engineering modules.
responsibilities: Progress exact approved artifacts through provider-neutral modules, gates, and trusted traceability.

elements.name: Generic Core
elements.description: Owns generic registration, state-derived routing, exact adapter resolution, checkpoints, replay, and progression.
responsibilities: Load exact state and artifact contracts.
Route without product-specific branches.
Checkpoint and replay bounded effects and control results.

elements.name: TraceabilityGraph
elements.description: Core-owned sidecar for trusted lifecycle traceability contributions and atomic merge proofs.
responsibilities: Replay approved upstream observer contributions.
Keep candidate and approved authority distinct.
Validate and atomically merge registered contributor updates.

elements.name: WorkBreakdown Module
elements.description: Converts exact approved scope into bounded, traceable, independently executable and verifiable work-item candidates.
responsibilities: Own establish-breakdown and decompose-change semantic contracts.
Normalize configured planning adapter output.
Return candidates without executing work.

elements.name: Context-neutral Upstream Validators
elements.description: Composes schema and semantic validators for requirements, project overview, architecture, contract, repository, and capability inputs without reusing ArchitectureDesign operation-specific runtime contracts.
responsibilities: Validate exact upstream artifacts in a WorkBreakdown-neutral context.
Enforce approved absence unions and cross-artifact lineage.

elements.name: Configured Planning Adapter Port
elements.description: Provider-neutral port for one bounded work-decomposition capability selected by configuration.
responsibilities: Invoke Spec Kit tasks, OpenSpec tasks, or a compatible planner through the same canonical contract.
Allow read and planning-artifact output only.

elements.name: Registered WorkBreakdown Preflight
elements.description: Generic guard registered on the loaded ProjectWorkBreakdownState artifact contract with its own persisted producer identity.
responsibilities: Detect exact baseline, disposition, revision, and tree drift before adapter entry.
Schema-validate baseline_drift results.
Checkpoint and replay the control result without adapter entry.

elements.name: WorkBreakdown Gate
elements.description: Derives the authoritative coverage universe, resolves evidence, owns no-work approval, and promotes approved planned work.
responsibilities: Reject unscoped or uncovered work.
Approve or reject already-satisfied and no-work-required dispositions.
Atomically promote a baseline or apply an exact typed delta.

elements.name: WorkBreakdown Traceability Contributor
elements.description: Trusted projector of validated candidate work items into limited planning relationships.
responsibilities: Create only approved planning edge kinds.

workItems.objective: Implement the closed ProjectMemory artifact, Gate, provider, conclusion, synopsis, and traceability contracts with strict validators.

included: Provider-neutral schemas and validators for all eight approved PM interface intents.
Exact references, content digests, authority, disposition, checkpoint, receipt, and failure semantics.
Positive, malformed, substitution, additional-property, and installed-package fixtures.
excluded: Provider-owned baseline, Gate, or TraceabilityGraph authority.

deliverables.description: PM-001 schemas, validators, exports, and conformance fixtures.

checks.method: Validate canonical positive artifacts and exhaustive malformed, stale, substituted, additional-property, cloned-receipt, and digest-mismatch fixtures.
checks.successCriteria: Every PM authority-bearing artifact validates only under its exact closed contract and cannot be inferred from chat or mutated by a provider.

required-evidence.description: Every PM authority-bearing artifact validates only under its exact closed contract and cannot be inferred from chat or mutated by a provider.

workItems.objective: Implement idempotent /conclude, explicit qualitative-delta review, atomic ProjectMemoryGate promotion, synopsis regeneration, and concurrent-worker coordination.

included: Typed add, replace, supersede, retain, and reject candidates presented after each wave or completed task.
Exact owner dispositions, compare-and-swap baseline promotion, journaled recovery, and idempotent ConcludeReceipt.
Candidate-only worker conclusions with parent-session serialized promotion.
excluded: Silent memory writes, worker baseline mutation, or model-inferred approval.

deliverables.description: /conclude coordinator, ProjectMemoryGate, atomic baseline store, synopsis projector, and recovery journal.

dependency-hints.rationale: Conclusion applies the finalized authority, history, and candidate semantics.
Conclude and recovery must invalidate and refresh the exact current context.

checks.method: Test approve, reject, partial disposition, stale baseline, concurrent workers, retry, crash recovery, duplicate conclude, synopsis failure, graph failure, and atomic rollback.
checks.successCriteria: Only exact user-approved qualitative deltas promote, retries are idempotent, concurrent workers cannot overwrite each other, and baseline, synopsis, graph, and receipt remain consistent.

required-evidence.description: Only exact user-approved qualitative deltas promote, retries are idempotent, concurrent workers cannot overwrite each other, and baseline, synopsis, graph, and receipt remain consistent.

workItems.objective: Load CurrentSynopsis and exact ProjectMemory context first for every configured fresh task and refresh it deterministically at module boundaries.

included: First semantic context load with synopsis, exact baselines, decisions, blockers, recent sessions, and relevant traceability context.
Task, workspace, repository revision, artifact versions, digests, cache behavior, and duration receipts.
Unconcluded-session detection with explicit resume, conclude, or abandon routing.
excluded: Unrelated ChatGPT chats, undocumented tab-close hooks, or conversational memory as a substitute for pinned inputs.

deliverables.description: Context assembler, mandatory startup/refresh hook, briefing projection, and load receipts.

dependency-hints.rationale: Bootstrap requires authoritative namespace and retrieval semantics.

checks.method: Exercise fresh task, new day, restart, warm/cold cache, stale binding, missing synopsis, open session, refresh, and unrelated-chat fixtures.
checks.successCriteria: No configured DevRelay task begins with stale or missing project context, and every successful load is reconstructable from an exact receipt.

required-evidence.description: No configured DevRelay task begins with stale or missing project context, and every successful load is reconstructable from an exact receipt.

workItems.objective: Integrate ProjectMemory, /conclude, Mem0 configuration, and startup recovery into the supported ChatGPT/Codex Desktop Windows workflow and public package surface.

included: DevRelay skill and command guidance that loads memory first and reminds or blocks on required conclusion.
Module/plugin catalogs, maturity records, package exports, examples, ProjectOverview, lifecycle reports, and operator documentation.
Explicit local-only defaults, opt-in network behavior, supported-host claims, and migration guidance.
excluded: A one-click ChatGPT plug-in, hosted memory backend, unsupported automatic tab-close interception, or public npm publication.

deliverables.description: Desktop hooks, skill/command assets, catalogs, exports, examples, reports, and operator documentation.

dependency-hints.rationale: Desktop configuration must bind the verified provider surface.
Skill and command behavior must match final conclusion semantics.
Reports and context guidance must match final graph projection behavior.

checks.method: Run catalog, package export, installed-package import, command/skill fixture, documentation-link, report-parity, and supported-host claim checks.
checks.successCriteria: A Windows Desktop user can discover and operate the exact ProjectMemory lifecycle without hidden authority, stale docs, or unsupported product claims.

required-evidence.description: A Windows Desktop user can discover and operate the exact ProjectMemory lifecycle without hidden authority, stale docs, or unsupported product claims.

workItems.objective: Implement and attest a pinned local Mem0 adapter as a bounded derived-memory provider behind the ProjectMemory provider port.

included: Pinned Windows-local Mem0 installation and capability negotiation.
Bounded add, search, update, and delete proposal operations with raw execution receipts and native artifact archival.
Outbound source or embedding transmission disabled by default and explicit opt-in enforcement.
excluded: Direct baseline, Gate, graph, filesystem-wide, or implicit network authority.

deliverables.description: Live-conformant local Mem0 adapter, manifest, receipts, and provider-failure fixtures.

dependency-hints.rationale: The provider is bounded by the finalized native authority and fallback boundary.

checks.method: Invoke the pinned local provider for every bounded operation, archive exact receipts, and test unavailable, malformed, stale, network-denied, substitution, and fallback cases.
checks.successCriteria: Mem0 is live-provider-attested on Windows, remains derived and replaceable, and provider failure cannot silently corrupt or bypass ProjectMemory authority.

required-evidence.description: Mem0 is live-provider-attested on Windows, remains derived and replaceable, and provider failure cannot silently corrupt or bypass ProjectMemory authority.

workItems.objective: Implement deterministic ProjectMemory routing, namespace management, authority precedence, retrieval, history, and verified native fallback.

included: Project, session, and invocation-scoped module namespaces with deterministic routing.
Authority-over-recency conflict resolution and append, replace, supersede, retain, and reject semantics.
Bounded retrieval, history preservation, checkpoint replay, and equivalent verified native fallback.
excluded: Treating modules as autonomous agents or raw chat as authoritative memory.

deliverables.description: Native ProjectMemory engine, router, stores, retrieval, precedence, and replay behavior.

dependency-hints.rationale: The native engine must emit and consume the finalized PM contracts.

checks.method: Run deterministic namespace, authority conflict, retrieval, history, fallback, malformed-state, and zero-call replay matrices.
checks.successCriteria: Identical pinned inputs produce byte-identical context and candidates, lower-authority recent claims never override approved facts, and failures are fail-closed.

required-evidence.description: Identical pinned inputs produce byte-identical context and candidates, lower-authority recent claims never override approved facts, and failures are fail-closed.

workItems.objective: Add exhaustive ProjectMemory determinism, security, mutation, concurrency, performance, and transition-safe regression coverage.

included: Property, mutation, negative, checkpoint, graph, provider, installed-package, and Windows matrices.
Cold/warm context-load and bounded retrieval budgets with raw command, duration, version, and fingerprint receipts.
Historical release-fixture isolation from mutable current baselines.
excluded: Weakening fail-closed behavior or rewriting historical digests to conceal drift.

deliverables.description: PM-001 complete regression, performance, security, concurrency, and mutation suites.

dependency-hints.rationale: The complete matrix verifies the integrated module, provider, package, reports, and Desktop surface.

checks.method: Run focused suites, mutation and concurrency matrices, repeated canonical-byte comparisons, performance samples, canonical verify, catalog verification, and installed-package verification.
checks.successCriteria: All PM failure modes and authority boundaries are covered, deterministic repeats match, budgets pass, and the complete prior release gate remains green.

required-evidence.description: All PM failure modes and authority boundaries are covered, deterministic repeats match, budgets pass, and the complete prior release gate remains green.

workItems.objective: Implement trusted TraceabilityGraph context projection and ProjectMemory contribution without exposing graph authority to Mem0 or other adapters.

included: Read-only projection from an approved graph checkpoint into bounded memory context.
Deterministic links from approved memory facts and decisions to source artifacts and lifecycle entities.
Compact provenance and impact queries for why, coverage, and affected-change questions.
excluded: Direct provider graph reads, arbitrary relationship types, inverse-edge storage, or candidate-authored graph operations.

deliverables.description: Trusted traceability projector, contributor, query context, merge proofs, and orphan diagnostics.

dependency-hints.rationale: The trusted projector and contributor require finalized trace contracts.
Projected graph context must enter the bounded native retrieval path.

checks.method: Validate exact checkpoint projection, provider isolation, allowed vocabulary, source provenance, orphan detection, atomic merge, replay, and compact query fixtures.
checks.successCriteria: Memory can explain lifecycle provenance from exact graph facts while no untrusted provider can access or mutate the graph.

required-evidence.description: Memory can explain lifecycle provenance from exact graph facts while no untrusted provider can access or mutate the graph.

workItems.objective: Prove ProjectMemory end to end from fresh and worker ChatGPT/Codex Desktop tasks on Windows using the packed DevRelay library and live local Mem0 provider.

included: Fresh configured task loads CurrentSynopsis first and reconstructs exact approved context.
A worker produces a candidate-only conclusion; the parent reviews qualitative deltas, approves selected changes, runs /conclude, and refreshes context.
Restart and resume prove baseline, synopsis, history, traceability, receipts, provider evidence, and zero-call replay.
excluded: Public npm publication, hosted backend, implicit external transmission, or unsupported automatic tab-close behavior.

deliverables.description: Clean Windows Desktop ProjectMemory dogfood, release evidence, lifecycle report, milestone, and acceptance package.

dependency-hints.rationale: The release-defining Desktop run requires the complete green regression, security, and performance gate.

checks.method: Run the complete installed-package scenario in fresh, worker, parent, concluded, restarted, and resumed Desktop tasks and reconstruct every exact artifact and receipt.
checks.successCriteria: A user can leave and resume DevRelay with accurate context, explicitly govern every qualitative change, and trace the resulting memory through the complete lifecycle without conversational-memory dependence.

required-evidence.description: A user can leave and resume DevRelay with accurate context, explicitly govern every qualitative change, and trace the resulting memory through the complete lifecycle without conversational-memory dependence.

workItem.objective: Implement closed EnvironmentPreparation profile, inventory, remediation, effect, verification, readiness, and traceability artifacts with strict validators.

included: Canonical schemas and validators for all seven EP interface intents.
Exact baseline, profile, fingerprint, grant, receipt, outcome, checkpoint, and evidence semantics.
Malformed, stale, substituted, additional-property, secret, and drift fixtures.

deliverables.description: EP-001 schemas, validators, exports, and conformance fixtures.

checks.method: Validate positive artifacts and exhaustive malformed, stale, substituted, additional-property, secret-value, and digest-mismatch fixtures.
checks.successCriteria: Every EP artifact validates only under its exact closed contract and no adapter can assert readiness or graph authority.

required-evidence.description: Every EP artifact validates only under its exact closed contract and no adapter can assert readiness or graph authority.

workItem.objective: Integrate environment profiles, remediation review, readiness status, and evidence into the supported ChatGPT/Codex Desktop Windows library and guidance.

included: Human-readable pre-effect display of mutations, grants, impact, rollback, checks, warnings, and evidence.
Module/plugin catalogs, package exports, examples, reports, ProjectOverview, operator documentation, and support claims.
Clear separation from deployment, staging success, ReleasePreparation, and public npm publication.
excluded: A one-click Desktop plug-in, hosted service, or unsupported host claim.

deliverables.description: Desktop-facing APIs, commands, catalogs, examples, reports, and operator documentation.

dependency-hints.rationale: Desktop behavior must match final Gate and readiness semantics.
Catalog and maturity guidance must reflect verified adapter behavior.

checks.method: Run package export, installed-package import, catalog, example, report parity, documentation link, support-claim, and Desktop interaction fixtures.
checks.successCriteria: A Windows Desktop user can understand, approve, remediate, verify, and audit the environment without hidden effects or stale claims.

required-evidence.description: A Windows Desktop user can understand, approve, remediate, verify, and audit the environment without hidden effects or stale claims.

workItem.objective: Implement the Core-owned EnvironmentVerificationGate and single-attempt readiness binding before every WorkExecution frontier.

included: Required/optional policy truth table and closed Gate outcomes.
Repository, baseline, profile, adapter, tool, host, target, frontier, work-item, assignment, and attempt binding.
Immediate fingerprint revalidation, drift handling, single-use receipts, and baseline establishment.
excluded: Changing the dependency DAG, assignment, schedule, or product work.

deliverables.description: EnvironmentVerificationGate, readiness binder, policy engine, baseline store, and drift/remediation routing.

dependency-hints.rationale: The Gate requires exact current profile facts and fingerprints.
Readiness evaluates the finalized preparation evidence and checkpoints.

checks.method: Test every Gate outcome, policy truth table, failed/unknown required checks, warning-only optional checks, drift, expiry, substitution, receipt reuse, frontier mismatch, and replay.
checks.successCriteria: WorkExecution cannot start without one exact current Gate-owned receipt and any material change invalidates that authorization.

required-evidence.description: WorkExecution cannot start without one exact current Gate-owned receipt and any material change invalidates that authorization.

workItem.objective: Implement capability-oriented optional inventory, acquisition, configuration, service-check, and target-probe adapter bindings with honest maturity.

included: Provider-neutral manifests and capability negotiation.
Exact version, configuration, grant, execution, evidence, failure, and substitution receipts.
Fixture, unavailable, malformed, and at least one live Windows conformance path where release claims require it.
excluded: Tool-specific Core routing or support claims without live evidence.

deliverables.description: Environment adapter SDK, manifests, bounded host executors, conformance suite, and maturity records.

dependency-hints.rationale: Adapters are bounded by the canonical EP request and receipt contracts.
Effect adapters require finalized grant, checkpoint, and rollback semantics.

checks.method: Run live and fixture conformance, unavailable, malformed output, provider substitution, undeclared effect, grant escalation, secret, network, and fallback matrices.
checks.successCriteria: Adapters remain swappable and untrusted, and maturity claims exactly match archived provider evidence.

required-evidence.description: Adapters remain swappable and untrusted, and maturity claims exactly match archived provider evidence.

workItem.objective: Implement consolidated remediation planning and safe, project-local, reversible, checkpointed preparation effects.

included: One ordered remediation wave for all required gaps.
Exact effects, grants, impact, rollback, idempotency, before/after fingerprints, and evidence obligations.
Crash-safe checkpoints and zero-effect replay.
excluded: Silent retries, implicit network access, unapproved machine-global changes, or work execution.

deliverables.description: Remediation planner, effect coordinator, rollback controller, checkpoint recovery, and mutation receipts.

dependency-hints.rationale: Remediation must be derived from exact observed profile gaps.

checks.method: Exercise approve, reject, partial grant, network-denied, global-mutation, rollback, crash, retry, stale fingerprint, secret, and idempotent replay cases.
checks.successCriteria: Only approved reversible effects execute, every transition is receipted, recovery is deterministic, and replay performs zero effects.

required-evidence.description: Only approved reversible effects execute, every transition is receipted, recovery is deterministic, and replay performs zero effects.

workItem.objective: Implement two-layer environment profiles, deterministic routing, and native Windows host inventory with exact redacted evidence.

included: DevRelay host plus named project profile resolution.
Required and optional checks for OS, architecture, shells, runtimes, package managers, SDKs, tools, services, environment variables, paths, and attestations.
Offline read-only Windows inventory with ignore, privacy, freshness, and support-claim controls.
excluded: Automatic remediation, machine-global mutation, or unproven project-technology support claims.

deliverables.description: Environment profile engine, operation router, native Windows inventory, fingerprints, and raw observation receipts.

dependency-hints.rationale: Profiles and observations must emit the finalized EP contracts.

checks.method: Run deterministic Windows inventory, profile selection, required/optional, redaction, attestation-expiry, unsupported-target, and zero-call replay matrices.
checks.successCriteria: The exact host and project requirements resolve deterministically and inventory produces complete redacted evidence without overstating support.

required-evidence.description: The exact host and project requirements resolve deterministically and inventory produces complete redacted evidence without overstating support.

workItem.objective: Add exhaustive environment determinism, security, mutation, recovery, drift, concurrency, telemetry, and transition-safe regression coverage.

included: Property, mutation, negative, permission, secret, network, path, rollback, crash, replay, graph, and installed-package matrices.
Bounded parallel read-check and serialized-effect tests.
Per-check duration, retries, cache hits, changed facts, command fingerprints, and bottleneck receipts without asserting a universal wall-clock SLA.
excluded: Weakening fail-closed behavior or rewriting historical evidence.

deliverables.description: EP-001 complete regression, security, recovery, concurrency, mutation, and telemetry suites.

dependency-hints.rationale: The complete matrix verifies the integrated runtime, adapters, package, reports, and Desktop surface.
The regression gate must include approved graph contribution and replay.

checks.method: Run focused, mutation, permission, security, crash, drift, concurrency, repeatability, telemetry, canonical verify, catalog, and installed-package suites.
checks.successCriteria: All EP failure modes and authority boundaries are covered, deterministic repeats match, telemetry is complete, and every prior release gate remains green.

required-evidence.description: All EP failure modes and authority boundaries are covered, deterministic repeats match, telemetry is complete, and every prior release gate remains green.

workItem.objective: Implement trusted forward traceability from profiles and readiness to work items, execution attempts, evidence, and graph checkpoints.

included: Trusted contributor vocabulary and deterministic graph updates.
Adapter isolation, endpoint validation, atomic merge, replay, merge proof, and orphan diagnostics.
Queryable provenance for why an environment check or preparation effect exists.
excluded: Adapter-authored graph operations, arbitrary relationships, or stored inverse edges.

deliverables.description: Environment traceability contributor, queries, updates, merge proofs, and diagnostics.

dependency-hints.rationale: The contributor requires finalized readiness and trace contracts.
Only Gate-approved readiness facts can enter the graph.

checks.method: Validate forward vocabulary, source closure, adapter isolation, unknown endpoints, atomic merge, replay, orphan detection, and provenance queries.
checks.successCriteria: Every approved readiness decision is reconstructable through the lifecycle while untrusted adapters have no graph authority.

required-evidence.description: Every approved readiness decision is reconstructable through the lifecycle while untrusted adapters have no graph authority.

workItem.objective: Prove EnvironmentPreparation and EnvironmentVerification end to end in a clean ChatGPT/Codex Desktop Windows run using the packed DevRelay library.

included: Establish exact host and project profiles, inventory current facts, expose a controlled gap, review and apply reversible remediation, and pass the Gate.
Begin one bound WorkExecution attempt, introduce drift, block reuse, remediate, reverify, and resume.
Archive raw commands, versions, grants, fingerprints, effects, rollback, readiness, graph, replay, and installed-package evidence.
excluded: Public npm publication, deployment, staging success, hosted backend, or unsupported target technology claims.

deliverables.description: Clean Windows Desktop environment-preparation dogfood, evidence, lifecycle report, milestone, and acceptance package.

dependency-hints.rationale: The release-defining Desktop run requires the complete green regression and security gate.

checks.method: Run the installed package through clean inventory, controlled remediation, readiness, execution binding, drift, blocked reuse, re-preparation, re-verification, recovery, and zero-effect replay.
checks.successCriteria: A Windows Desktop user can safely prepare and prove the exact environment before execution, detect drift, recover deterministically, and trace every decision and effect.

required-evidence.description: A Windows Desktop user can safely prepare and prove the exact environment before execution, detect drift, recover deterministically, and trace every decision and effect.
